court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: Bharat Pertoleum Corporation Ltd vs Sree Venkateswara Service Station

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Bharat Pertoleum Corporation Ltd, Territory Manager and Chief Divisional Manager
parties.respondent_defendant: Sree Venkateswara Service Station, a regd. Firm

facts_of_case: The dealer entered into an agreement with the Petroleum Corporation for two retail outlets. The dealer was served with show cause notice and order of suspension. Three suits were filed by the dealer. Original Applications were filed by the dealer for grant of interim injunction.

legal_principles.principle: When a dealership agreement has come to an end by efflux of time, the issue raised in O.S.A.No.67 of 2001 becomes infructuous.
legal_principles.held: In view of the fact that the dealership agreement has now come to an end by efflux of time and the agreement is no more in force, we are not deliberating on the issue raised in O.S.A.No.67 of 2001, which became infructuous.

legal_principles.principle: A show cause notice issued by the Petroleum Corporation, calling upon the dealer to give reply as to why his dealership agreement be not terminated, is a procedural step that must be followed.
legal_principles.held: Though explanation is called for by issuing the show cause notice, from the petitioner and explanation was offered by the petitioner denying the allegations...

outcome.final_order: The defendants are directed to supply petroleum products to the plaintiff subject to certain conditions.
